label: FY2027 Q2 (May–Jul 2026)
asOf: prices as of the 27 Oct 2026 close
headline: AI lit up security demand, but the stock is running twice as fast as ARR

points.t: $333M, +51% y/y; full-year net new ARR growth raised to about 34%.
Customers on Falcon Flex have $2.29B of ARR, doubled; converted customers raise ARR by more than 40% on average.
Up 20% the day after the report; enterprise value is now about 51x trailing revenue, above the 2021 peak.

reaction: Stock: closed at $189.18 on report day and +20.5% ($227.96) the next day, giving back 4.2% on the third day. The rally came from net new ARR clearly above guidance, another full-year raise, and the market's view that AI deployments drive security spending first (what management called lasting demand after Mythos). It kept rising and closed at $268.02 on 27 Oct, another 17.6% above the day after the report. Expectations are publicly reported consensus (Yahoo Finance). After the 4-for-1 split on 1 Jul 2026, prices above are post-split.

segments.title: By segment
segments.take: Growth came almost entirely from subscriptions; professional services is a supporting act.

rows.why: Subscription gross margin 81% (non-GAAP), versus 80% a year ago. Management targets 82–85% by FY29.
Incident response and consulting, a quarterly record, at lower margins.

segments.note: CrowdStrike does not report revenue by product; product lines only disclose ARR, broken down below.

extras.title: ARR breakdown
extras.take: New products beyond the endpoint each have several hundred million dollars of ARR, all growing faster than the company.

items.w: A credit-based, use-as-you-go model. 34% of this quarter's net new ARR came from new customers on Flex.
Protects workloads in the cloud; the largest new product line.
Log and security analytics, taking share from legacy SIEM vendors.
Protects enterprise AI apps and agents, billed by token credits consumed through Flex. Still small; no dollar figure disclosed.

trends.why: A record after Q1's dip; Q3 guided at $343–347M
Q1 is the seasonal high; Q2 back to $377M

valuation.take: Enterprise value is about 51x trailing revenue, the highest in five years and above 46x in 2021. At its five-year median of about 21x, the current price needs revenue to more than double again from FY27: the price is supported by a story about the future, not by money already earned.

forward.title: The company already gives full-year EPS
steps: Full-year guide of $1.25–1.26 → implied Q4 about $0.36
forward.note: GAAP EPS was only $0.01 this quarter; the gap is mainly stock-based compensation. This is company guidance, not our forecast.

head: Case

scenarios.note: Base is the FY27 guided revenue midpoint of $6.0B; market cap about $282B. Even in the bull case, FY28 market cap / free cash flow is still above 100x. *Price: if the market pays the five-year median EV/revenue of 21.4x, the current price needs revenue of about $13.0B, about 116% above FY27. The price sits outside all three scenarios and needs several more years of high growth to grow into. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.sub: Enterprise value / revenue at quarter ends
history.note: About 51x now, above every one of the last 20 quarter ends, the 100th percentile. The last time it came close was 46x at the end of October 2021, after which it fell to 10x within a year. GAAP profit is too thin for P/E to mean anything, so we use EV/revenue. StockAnalysis data; quarter ends are fiscal quarter ends (end of January, April, July, October).

cash.title: Stock compensation vs free cash flow

stats.k: Q2 GAAP vs non-GAAP operating income gap

cash.note: A GAAP operating loss of $33M this quarter against $372M of non-GAAP operating income; the $405M gap is mainly stock-based compensation. The stock given to employees in one quarter was worth more than that quarter's free cash flow, continuously diluting shareholders. Management guides full-year free cash flow margin of at least 30%.

calc: Price $268.02: 27 Oct close; market cap ≈ $282B (about 1.05B shares from StockAnalysis market cap ÷ price), net cash about $4.2B, EV about $277B
Around the report: price × 1.205, TTM revenue × 1.059 → multiple × 1.138
Scenario free cash flow = FY28 revenue × free cash flow margin

changes.before: FY27 net new ARR growth of about 27.7%.
changes.now: About 34%, midpoint up 6.3 points; Q3 alone $343–347M net new.
Stresses that enterprises must solve AI security and compliance before they dare deploy, and calls the post-Mythos demand lasting, not one-off.
AI detection and response is billed by tokens: plans include an allowance, with token packs for overage consumed through Flex.
The XM Cyber technology asset acquisition is expected to close in the second half, excluded from ARR and revenue guidance.
Subscription gross margin of 82–85% by FY29; FY27 free cash flow margin of at least 30%.

insider.title: Effective trades 30 days around the report
insider.text: In the 30 days around the report (7/27–9/25), there was only one effective sale: director Cary Davis sold about $7.4M. Everything else was planned or tax-withholding sales, which we don't count: CFO Burt Podbere sold about $126M under a 10b5-1 plan, CEO George Kurtz about $114M in planned batches, and director Gerhard Watzinger about $29M. No insider bought. Management's planned sales were large while the stock surged, but those plans were set in advance. Data from April's Stock Atlas insider activity.
